title: [Suite autour de Teichmüller dont] Teichmülleries, 1981-1982 : notes manuscrites (1981-1983, s.d.), lettres (1981, s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page sits inside Grothendieck's 'Teichmülleries' (1981-82). It works on the two lowest levels of the Teichmüller tower: the extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus, Γ_{1,1}^{±} ≅ GL_2(Z), and its relation to the genus-0 / modular side (PGL_2(Z), the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group generated by reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞).

(1) Presentation via the square torus. The generators are:
- τ', τ'': two orientation-reversing involutions, the reflections of the square torus C/Z[i] in its two axes;
- σ: the rotation by a quarter turn (multiplication by i);
- ρ', ρ'': the Dehn twists (transvections) along the two axis curves.

The stated relations are:
- τ'^2 = τ''^2 = σ^4 = 1 and σ^2 = τ'τ''. Two perpendicular reflections compose to the half-turn -1, so <σ, τ', τ''> is the dihedral group D_4 of order 8. This is Aut of the square lattice together with complex conjugation, i.e. the stabiliser of the point i in GL_2(Z).
- τ'ρ'τ'^{-1} = τ''ρ'τ''^{-1} = ρ'^{-1}, and similarly for ρ''. A reflection preserving a curve inverts the twist along it.
- σρ'σ^{-1} = ρ'', hence σρ''σ^{-1} = ρ'^{±1}.
- A braid-type relation (σρ')^3 = 1 'dans Γ_{1,1}^+', with the parenthetical '(mais non dans un groupe spécial)'. Grothendieck is noting that this relation is sign- and convention-dependent. With S of order 4 and T a transvection, ST has order 3 or 6 depending on whether T or T^{-1} is used. In a central extension (e.g. the braid group B_3, or SL_2 versus PSL_2) it fails or holds only up to the centre.

(2) A homomorphism to the 'modular' generators. The assignments are:
- ρ' ↦ ε_0 and ρ'' ↦ ε_1 (the two elementary transvections);
- τ'' ↦ τ_∞ = τ = r_∞;
- τ' ↦ ω_0 τ_∞ = -τ, where ω_0 = -1 is central;
- σ ↦ σ_∞ = σ.

Derived elements:
- σ^{-1}ρ' = σ^3ρ' ↦ σ^3 ε_0 = σ^3(σρ) = ρ, using ε_0 = σρ and σ^4 = 1. Here ρ is the order-3 element.
- τ''σ ↦ τ'_∞ = r_0, which forces σ = r_∞ r_0.
- τ''ρ' = (τ''σ)(σ^{-1}ρ') ↦ r_0 ρ = r_1, consistent with ρ = r_0 r_1.

The boxed table records the dictionary, mapping the generators of the square-torus presentation to the three reflections r_∞, r_0, r_1 and to (ε_0, σ, ρ):
- τ'' ↦ r_∞, τ''σ ↦ r_0, τ''ρ' ↦ r_1;
- ρ' ↦ ε_0, σ ↦ σ, σ^{-1}ρ' ↦ ρ.

In effect this checks that GL_2(Z) is generated by the D_4 symmetry of the square torus plus one twist, and matches the classical extended-triangle-group description.

(3) Geometric/combinatorial model. 𝓧 = (X, X', X'') is a torus X with two further structures X', X''. These are plausibly the two real structures / reflection classes, or the two 'axes'; the sketch shows a torus with two dashed real circles. The square has vertices a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3, axes e (horizontal, the fixed axis of τ' = id) and e'' (vertical, where τ'' = ct, i.e. conjugation). This is the pillowcase or 2-torsion picture of the torus. Grothendieck identifies canonical finite sets attached to 𝓧:
- ℰ(𝓧) ↔ the set of codiagonals of the square;
- ε_0(X') ↔ the pair of opposite sides corresponding to X'';
- ε_1(X') ↔ the pair of opposite sides corresponding to X'.
He then records canonical bijections: vertices ≃ ε_0(X')×ε_1(X') ≃ ε_1(X'')×ε_0(X'') ≃ ε_0(X')×ε_0(X'') ≃ ε_1(X')×ε_1(X''). So the 4 special points (2-torsion points / branch points of X → P^1) form the product of two 2-element sets in several canonical ways. This is the kind of 'anabelian' bookkeeping of torsor structures that underlies the passage between level-2 structures on the elliptic curve and the 4 marked points on P^1 (Legendre picture, Γ_{1,1} versus Γ_{0,4}).
errors: The relation (σρ')^3 = 1 depends on whether ρ' is the twist or its inverse. With S of order 4 and T = [[1,1],[0,1]], (ST)^3 = -1 while (ST^{-1})^3 = 1. Grothendieck's parenthetical shows he is aware the relation is fragile; it is not an outright error.

The line 'τ' ↦ ω_0 τ_∞ = -τ' presupposes a target containing -1 (GL_2 rather than PGL_2), while the later table uses PGL_2-style reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞. The images are therefore consistent only modulo ±1 or with careful sign tracking, and the page does not make this explicit.

Read straight from the page, 'σ(ρ') = ρ'' ⇒ σ(ρ'') = ρ'' is only true up to inversion. σ^2 = -1 is central, so σ^2(ρ') = ρ' and hence σ(ρ'') = ρ'. But the identification of ρ'' with a twist along the 'other' axis may introduce ρ'^{-1}, depending on orientation conventions.

ideas.what: Presentation of GL_2(Z) ≅ Γ_{1,1}^± from the dihedral symmetry group D_4 of the square torus together with Dehn twists along the two axes
ideas.modern_name: presentation of the extended mapping class group of the once-punctured torus / GL_2(Z) as an amalgam of finite stabilisers
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke; Serre's 'Trees' for amalgam presentations)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses Γ_{1,1}, Γ_{0,4} and generation of the Teichmüller tower by low levels, but not this explicit presentation

ideas.what: Dictionary from torus generators (τ', τ'', σ, ρ', ρ'') to reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞ of the extended (2,3,∞) triangle group and elements ε_0, ε_1, ρ, σ
ideas.modern_name: PGL_2(Z) as the extended modular triangle group generated by three reflections

ideas.what: Canonical decomposition of the set of 4 special points (2-torsion / pillowcase vertices) as a product of two 2-element sets attached to the two structures X', X''
ideas.modern_name: level-2 structure / Klein four-group torsor of 2-torsion points; Legendre correspondence between M_{1,1}[2] and M_{0,4}
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Legendre family); in the anabelian context Grothendieck, Esquisse (1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (on Γ_{0,4} versus Γ_{1,1})

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful working-out of classical facts: a presentation of GL_2(Z) from the square torus's D_4 symmetry plus twists, and its match with the reflection-triangle description of PGL_2(Z). It also records the canonical combinatorics of the 4 special points of the pillowcase. It is useful insight into Grothendieck's working style for the low levels of the Teichmüller tower, but nothing appears beyond known material.
transcription_corrections: The symbol in '(σρ')^3 ? 1 dans Γ_{1,1}^+' is ambiguous in the image: it could be '=', '≃' or '≠'. 'mais non' (inserted above the line) is followed by 'dans un groupe spécial'.
In 'τ''=ct' under the square, 'ct' plausibly abbreviates conjugation or 'constant'; it is uncertain.
The square's axes are labelled e'' (vertical) and e (horizontal), with τ'=id on the horizontal axis; the vertex labels a_0, a_1, a_2, a_3 are as in the transcription.
In the line 'τ''σ ↦ τ'_∞ = r_0' the target is written τ'_∞, i.e. the primed counterpart of τ_∞.
